game.title: Internet History & Meme Origins
game.description: From the first email to Baby Yoda — a tour through the weird, wonderful history of the internet and the culture it created.

questions.prompt: The first email ever sent was sent by Ray Tomlinson in 1971, and he chose the '@' symbol to separate the username from the host computer.
The very first video uploaded to YouTube (April 2005) was a short clip of co-founder Jawed Karim at the San Diego Zoo.
The 'Rickrolling' internet prank tricks someone into clicking a link that plays 'Never Gonna Give You Up' by which artist? (First and last name)
Google's name originated as a misspelling of 'googol' — the mathematical term for the number 1 followed by 100 zeros.
In what year did Apple release the original iPhone, fundamentally changing how people access the internet?
Jack Dorsey's very first tweet in 2006 read 'just setting up my ___' — naming the platform by its original codename. What was the word?
The viral 'Keep Calm and Carry On' poster that spawned thousands of internet parodies was originally created by which government for which purpose?

options: The US government, to boost morale during the Great Depression
The British government, as a WWII motivational poster in 1939
A British design studio, as a satirical commentary in 2000
The Churchill War Rooms, as a souvenir for museum visitors

questions.prompt: Wikipedia was founded in 2001, meaning it is older than Facebook, YouTube, Twitter, and the iPhone.
Which of these describes your current relationship with social media?

options: Chronically online — I check it constantly
Casual scroller — a few times a day
Mostly lurker — I watch but rarely post

questions.prompt: Which of the following websites were launched BEFORE Facebook (February 2004)? Select all that apply.
Which of these internet slang abbreviations emerged from early 2000s online chat and message boards? Select all that apply.
Which social media platforms do you actively use right now? Select all that apply.
